newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa strikes pay deal with union.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa strikes pay deal with union.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG struck a two-year pay deal in the early hours of Friday with one of the two unions representing its 50,000 workers.
Just hours after the airline's wage talks with white collar union DAG collapsed, Lufthansa and its agreed on a new wage contract with the OeTV public sector union.
The deal, which runs through the end of 1998, involves one-time payments to workers to cover the period through March 30, 1998, and a 1.7 percent wage rise to the end of 1998.
The new contracts apply immediately to all Lufthansa staff, but negotiations with the DAG are to resume next month to secure its approval.
A spokeswoman for Lufthansa said the airline had never before struck separate deals with its unions.
DAG representatives told Reuters on Thursday that Lufthansa's wage offer was unacceptable and would leave workers with pay rises below the rate of inflation.
